attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-24
attempts.entry_title: Thalamic, mPFC and CA1 activity in non-REM sleep events (Varela and Wilson 2020)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held only in part here, and the maze findings could not be tested. SWR locking to mPFC delta and spindle phase reproduced, and SWR rate rose around K-complexes, but the thalamic rebound after them was only partly seen. Thalamic firing did not fall at SWRs or track SWR rate (1 of 3 units against 61.7%), and units were not less rhythmic than multi-unit activity. These results rest on 3 of the paper's 32 sessions and 5 thalamic units. Every comparison of sleep before and after the maze is untestable because the dataset holds no maze or pre-maze sleep.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Varela and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-24, which holds three of the paper's sessions from three rats (units, tetrode multi-unit activity and LFP from midline thalamus, mPFC and CA1, with derived sleep periods, K-complexes, spindle troughs and SWRs). It tests the timing and phase of SWRs around mPFC K-complexes and spindles, the firing of units of the three regions around these events, and, in the session of sleep after maze exploration, how CA1 units labelled as active on the maze take part in spindle cycles and SWRs. The sleep before the maze, the maze epoch, position data and most of the paper's units are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Varela and Wilson (2020) from CRCNS hc-24

outcomes.notes: No scaling of the scalogram meets both parts of the criterion. Relative to the state's mean power, the trough-triggered mPFC scalogram in sleep peaks at 11 Hz (S1) and 10 Hz (S3) under every trough reading, within 10 to 15 Hz, but CA1 troughs detected outside sleep peak at 13 Hz in S1 (sleep 11 to 12 Hz) and 9 to 10 Hz in S3 (sleep 9 Hz), so the waking CA1 peak is not lower. In raw power the S3 waking CA1 peak is lower (7 against 8 Hz) but the S3 mPFC sleep peak is at 4 to 8 Hz. Outside sleep is all time outside the deposited sleep periods in the box (97 to 488 troughs), which includes any REM sleep; no active waking on the maze is in the data set. Up to 800 troughs per condition (seeded subset). Question for the authors, recorded as a finding: how the scalogram of Figure 1, figure supplement 3 was normalised.
deviations: Wavelet power shown both raw and relative to the mean power of the same LFP in the same state at each frequency; the paper does not say how the scalogram is scaled. The outcome is the same under both.
Morlet wavelet of 7 cycles (the claims files standard choice); 2 to 30 Hz in 1 Hz steps.
Waking is time outside the deposited sleep periods in the box only, including any REM sleep; the paper also used the maze.

Sleep is the deposited sleep periods (M-sleep reading a). The Methods rule as written (readings b and c, 1 s and 10 s averages) finds no sleep in S1 and S3 and at most 2 min in S2 (shown under fig3a-thalamic-rate-wake-sleep), so it cannot replace them.

All within -0.04 +- 0.43 and -1.72 +- 0.93; raw phases agree. Per-session Rayleigh Z 45 to 205 (p < 1e-19). Measured is the first reading the criterion lists (M-SWR k = 3).

outcomes.notes: Five thalamic units, deposited sleep periods (M-sleep reading a), waking reading (a). outcomes.notes: Three CA1, three mPFC and two thalamic tetrodes. All CA1 and mPFC tetrodes reach z 3 in -100 to 100 ms of spindle troughs under every trough reading (z 6.0 to 32.2), the thalamic tetrodes 2 of 2 (deposited troughs) or 1 of 2; the strongest modulation is on an mPFC tetrode (z 22.0 to 32.2), so the order CA1 > mPFC > thalamus fails. outcomes.notes: Five thalamic units, MUA on 2 tetrodes (S1, S3; 21 subsampled curves). The peak is the maximum after the first minimum that follows lag 0, the curve smoothed by 0, 1 or 2 bins to find that minimum; on a synthetic 10 Hz process it is at 100 ms under every bin and smoothing. Mean peak lag: units 30 to 160 ms, MUA 32 to 194 ms across bins, smoothings and MUA readings; Mann-Whitney p = 0.15 to 1.0, so units are not later. Subsampled MUA curves peaking in the spindle band 5 to 52 % (against 63.3 +- 6.33), units 0 to 60 %, MUA higher in 3 of 12 readings. Peak values in the band: MUA 0.025 to 0.048, units 0.033 to 0.094. The unit lags move with the smoothing (S2 cl-1 from 30 to 335 ms), as their first minimum often falls at 5 to 10 ms after the burst lags. Measured: all MUA spikes (A), 5 ms bins, no smoothing, band (ii), as band (i) leaves the unit value undefined.
deviations: Sleep spikes are those in the deposited sleep periods; the deposited script AutocorrelogramUnitMUA.mlx uses spikes within 2.5 s of KCs instead, not run here.

outcomes.notes: Three thalamic units with CA1 (S1, S3). Modulation index from the peri-trough histogram smoothed over +-1 s and cropped to -100..100 ms; flat Poisson firing at the same troughs gives 0.06 to 0.17, the units 0.18 to 0.75 over all cycles. Higher index in high ripple power cycles: 1 of 3 units (33.3 %) with the deposited and the Methods troughs, 0 of 3 with the Results troughs (against 64.52 +- 6.45); with S3's deposited high and low labels 1 of 2. More modulated in low cycles (the 22.58 % subset): 66.7, 33.3 and 0 %. No reading has a majority increasing. The two S3 units differ by 0.03 to 0.08 between high and low cycles with the deposited troughs, about the 0.07 to 0.10 index flat firing gives at the same troughs, so their direction is within the noise; only the S1 unit's decrease (0.67 against 0.82) is clearly larger. outcomes.notes: Three units, rated on values and directions (proposed after verification round 2, agreed in round 3). Index higher for high amplitude cycles in 3, 2 and 2 of 3 units across readings (mean change +0.14, +0.12 and +0.09), for high ripple power in 1, 1 and 0 of 3 (mean change -0.030, -0.125 and -0.134), for the joint split in 3, 3 and 0 of 3. The amplitude effect goes the paper's way and is larger than the ripple effect in every reading. With 3 units the smallest two-sided Wilcoxon p is 0.25 (p = 0.25 to 0.75), so neither the significant amplitude effect nor the contrast can be shown, and the similarity tests (p = 0.25 to 1.0) carry no information at this n. Evidence for similar absolute values is only the median absolute difference of high-cycle indices, 0.017 to 0.063; the mean high-cycle index is higher under the amplitude split in every reading (0.48 against 0.42, 0.67 against 0.50, 0.53 against 0.40). The S3 units' amplitude changes with the deposited troughs (0.12 and 0.13) are close to the 0.07 to 0.10 that flat firing gives. Amplitude is reading (a) only; reading (b) moves with it in every session (spindle-cycles-by-ripple-power).

outcomes.notes: Too few units for the claim's tests (3 units; no Wilcoxon test can reach p < 0.05). In the top amplitude quartile 33.3 to 66.7 % of units increase with ripple power (mean increase 24.5 to 65.1 %), in the top ripple power quartile 66.7 to 100 % increase with amplitude (15.9 to 65.5 %); ripple effect p = 0.5 to 1.0, amplitude effect p = 0.25 to 1.0; Spearman correlation of the two changes negative in 5 of 6 readings (rho -1.0 to 0.5). The 61.29 +- 6.13 band holds 66.7 % and the 32.26 +- 3.23 band holds 33.3 %, so both can be met with 3 units (an earlier version of this note said neither could); three of the four values are within tolerance in two readings, and the amplitude percentage in none. Amplitude is reading (a) of spindle-cycles-by-ripple-power only. The outcome stays blocked; the proposed change to not_reproduced was not agreed in verification round 3.

proposed.reason: Rated on values and directions, as for the other claims at this n. The share of units that increase with amplitude in the top ripple power quartile is 66.7 to 100 %, outside 32.26 +- 3.23 in every reading; at least as many units increase with amplitude as with ripple power in every reading, where the paper has 61 % against 32 %; and the Spearman correlation the paper reports as positive (0.51) is negative in 5 of 6 readings, though with 3 units rho takes only four values. No reading meets the claim's pattern. Notebook, cells of fig6e-quartile-synergy. Verifier, round 3, disagrees and would give partially_reproduced: the parts of the claim split both ways. The amplitude percentage and the sign of rho fail, but the ripple percentage (66.7 % in 5 of 6 readings) and its mean increase (4 of 6 readings) are within tolerance, three of four values are within tolerance in two readings, and the mean amplitude change exceeds the ripple change in the deposited and Methods readings. It reads "at least as many units increase with amplitude as with ripple power" as counting the failed amplitude percentage a second time, and "no reading meets the claim's pattern" as true also of the two claims rated partial.

outcomes.notes: Three units, rated on values and directions (proposed after verification round 2, agreed in round 3). The upper-quartile amplitude index is above the ripple power one in every reading (2 or 3 of 3 units). Mean upper-quartile index 0.51 to 0.93 for amplitude, within 1.16 +- 0.57 in the Methods (0.93) and Results (0.71) readings and outside it with the deposited troughs (0.51), and 0.46 to 0.55 for ripple power, within 0.60 +- 0.26 in every reading (Mann-Whitney p = 0.4 to 0.7). Spread ratio, quartile against median split, 1.18 to 2.37 for amplitude and 0.79 to 1.39 for ripple power, larger for amplitude in 5 of 6 readings; the ripple power ratio is also above 1 in 4 of 6 readings, so the quartile split widens the spread for both and more for amplitude. F-tests p = 0.37 to 0.86 (amplitude) and 0.73 to 0.98 (ripple power). The quartile split raises the index more than the median split in 33.3 to 100 % of units for amplitude and 33.3 to 66.7 % for ripple power; 3 units allow no percentage inside the 29 +- 2.9 and 22.6 +- 2.26 bands, and Mann-Whitney on 3 against 3 cannot give p below 0.1. Amplitude is reading (a) only.

findings.statement: The data set holds 3 recording sessions (about 3.5 h, 5 thalamic units) of the paper's 32 sessions with thalamic units (63 thalamic units). It holds no maze epoch, no sleep before the maze, none of the four long control sessions and no position (LED) data, so the paper's comparisons of sleep before and after the maze (six claims) and the waking definition by velocity cannot be tested, and most unit-level claims rest on 2 to 13 units.

The thalamic nucleus of each unit is not given; only the Session 1 unit is named (MD), in the title of a deposited script. Session 2's two units sit in a folder with no region in its name and are thalamic only by the deposited script's title. The LFP files state no unit, and the descriptor does not say which tetrode and wire each LFP comes from.

The deposited spindle troughs do not follow the detection rule of the Methods (local minima three sd below the mean of the spindle-filtered LFP): they are 3.7 to 6.2 times as many as that rule gives (3817 against 1019 in Session 1) and their filtered values reach -0.7 to -1.1 sd. The deposited Session 1 SWRs (1263) are also more than the Methods' k = 3 rule gives (840). Question for the authors: what threshold and reference period produced the deposited troughs and SWRs, and were these the events behind the paper's figures?

Question for the authors: how was the spindle-trough-triggered scalogram of Figure 1, figure supplement 3 scaled (raw wavelet power, or power relative to a baseline)? This attempt shows both raw power and power relative to the mean power of the same state; in raw power the Session 3 mPFC peak falls at 4 to 8 Hz, not 10 to 15 Hz.

Spike times are stored at single precision. In Session 3 every spike time equals its float32 rounding, a resolution of 2^-10 s (0.98 ms) at these values, which produces repeated timestamps (6230 in the thalamic MUA, 657 in the mPFC MUA, 17 and 8 in two thalamic units); in Sessions 1 and 2, 73 to 87 % of times do. LFP and event times are in double precision.

In Session 3 the mPFC unit and MUA start at 11750 s, 24 min before the LFP, the sleep periods and every other stream (13200 s); the descriptor does not say what this epoch is. The CA1 files labelled "InRun" hold only spikes of the sleep after the maze; the maze spikes behind the label are not included.

The paper's Data availability statement names the CRCNS data set "HC-24" (doi:10.6080/K0K35RVG) and then says that the data set and the documentation that describes it are available as "HC-19" (crcns.org/data-sets/hc/hc-19). The hc-24 data descriptor (version 0.6) cites the 2019 bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/653436), not the eLife paper.

The Methods' sleep rule, mPFC delta power and CA1 ripple power both above the session mean for at least 2 min, finds no sleep in Sessions 1 and 3 when power is a 1 s or 10 s moving average of the squared filtered LFP, against 42 and 78 min of deposited sleep. Filling dips shorter than 30 s finds 19 and 44 min inside the deposited periods. Question for the authors: what smoothing, and what tolerance for short dips, produced the deposited sleep periods?

disagreements.reason: The sleep mPFC peak is at 10 to 11 Hz only after the author's normalisation; raw S3 power peaks at 4 to 8 Hz. The criterion needs the waking CA1 peak to be lower than in sleep, and it is not: S1 13 vs 11 to 12 Hz, S3 9 to 10 vs 9 Hz. fig1s3 waking is all time outside the non-REM periods, which includes REM.
No reading has all five values within tolerance. The SWR minimum falls 37 to 45 ms before the KC, where the paper has 10 ms after.

Sleep rate is lower in 5 of 5 units, but p = 0.0625, the smallest p possible at n = 5. Waking 10.30 is within tolerance. Sleep 4.58 is just outside the band, whose lower edge is 4.64. M-sleep readings (b) and (c), the author's own sleep detection, were not run; the sleep definition could change that outcome.
Burst percentage is higher in sleep in 5 of 5 units (p = 0.0625). The sleep fraction (80%) and both means are within tolerance. The waking fraction is 0% against a band of 22.5 to 27.5%.
The SWR-window means (18.9 and 19.9%) are within tolerance and above sleep in 3 of 3 units. Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.177.
Fewer spikes at SWRs in 2 of 3 units; burst % higher in 2 or 3 of 3. With 3 units the Wilcoxon p cannot go below 0.25. swr-shift-control uses one random shift per SWR.
The direction fails. Pure increase is the largest class (2 of 3 units, both in S3) and decrease covers 1 of 3. The criterion needs decreasing units to be the largest group.

The notebook marks this blocked, but under the methods KCs with disjoint groups: after only 40% (in band), both 20% (in band), before only 20% (out), and more units peak after than before. With the deposited KCs it is a 40/40 tie.

The notebook marks this blocked, but the order CA1 > mPFC > thalamus fails. All mPFC tetrodes pass, as do all CA1 tetrodes, and the strongest modulation is in mPFC (z 22 to 32). CA1 at 100% is out of band.

The outputs fail: Mann-Whitney p >= 0.69 and MUA in-band 14 to 19% against 63%. But the peak finder takes the global minimum within 0 to 200 ms, where the criterion says the minimum that follows lag 0; on a synthetic 10 Hz process it returns a 200 ms peak, so this does not test the claim. It asked for per-curve autocorrelograms with the first local minimum marked, and the lags recomputed with it.
Mean peak z is 4.56 or 7.24 against 2.40 +- 1.21, and both pairs exceed 3 sd. These are 2 deposited example pairs.

In-cycle z is above between-spindle z in 2 of 2 pairs, and the between value (2.98) is within tolerance. The in-cycle value (6.75) is outside, and the test cannot be run with 2 pairs. Both spike trains are restricted to the same roughly 100 ms cycles, which by construction puts extra pairs at short lags; no control was run, for example cycle-shuffled trains.

Circular mean 1.18 rad (reading a) is within tolerance, and all 5 units have a positive mean phase. The significant fraction is 60% against a band of 60.97 to 74.51%. fig5c-spindle is blocked while fig5c-delta is tested, although both have the same 20% granularity.
p is 0.31 to 1.0 in both bands, but with n = 5 the smallest possible p is 0.0625, so the test cannot reject (uninformative).

Deposited reading: 2 of 3 units (66.7%) are in band; the methods and results readings give 33% (unreliable). The 22.58% subset is never computed, and the modulation index is biased: it smooths a +-100 ms histogram with mode same, so flat Poisson firing gives an index of 0.39 where it should be about 0. The histogram should be smoothed over a wider range and then cropped.

With n = 3 neither test can reach significance (uninformative). No test or median difference was printed, and with the deposited troughs spikes per cycle are higher in high-power cycles in 3 of 3 units.
All four means are within the wide tolerances. The 1 s decrease appears in the deposited and results means but not in the methods reading. Tests are impossible at n = 3.
Coupled > uncoupled for CA1 in 3 of 3 tetrodes and mPFC in 2 to 3 of 3; thalamus shows no consistent change. With 3 tetrodes p cannot go below 0.25.
The ripple-power main effect is significant (p 0.001 to 0.017) and run units have higher means. The run effect is not significant: Mann-Whitney p >= 0.2, ANOVA run p >= 0.12.

entries.name: crcns-hc-24-varela-2020
entries.title: Thalamic, mPFC and CA1 activity in non-REM sleep events (Varela and Wilson 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Varela and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-24, which holds three of the paper's sessions from three rats (units, tetrode multi-unit activity and LFP from midline thalamus, mPFC and CA1, with derived sleep periods, K-complexes, spindle troughs and SWRs). It tests the timing and phase of SWRs around mPFC K-complexes and spindles, the firing of units of the three regions around these events, and, in the session of sleep after maze exploration, how CA1 units labelled as active on the maze take part in spindle cycles and SWRs. The sleep before the maze, the maze epoch, position data and most of the paper's units are not in the data set.
